Uses distances and an explicit symmetric Gram determinant instead of the signed coordinate determinant computation in the original certificate.
correctness.rationale: For each unordered four-vertex selection, the squared absolute edge-vector determinant is the determinant of its three-by-three Gram matrix; polarization obtains every entry from the six squared distances. Independent exact enumeration in Q(phi), phi²=phi+1, over all 4,845 selections reproduces the eleven magnitudes d=6V, in order, with counts 495, 320, 900, 1110, 120, 900, 400, 150, 320, 120, 10. All algebraic ordering comparisons are exact, and squaring is injective on nonnegative magnitudes. The maximum 16 and runner-up 8phi occur 10 and 120 times; both squared-edge biconditionals were tested on every selection. The volume gap is 4(2−phi)/3. Allowing arbitrary points in the solid preserves the absolute maximum because the signed affine determinant is separately affine in its four points, hence a convex combination of signed vertex-supported values; that reasoning does not give a continuous runner-up.
residual_risks: The classification uses exactly the displayed coordinates and counts unordered vertex subsets, including coplanar subsets. In other normalizations volumes scale cubically.
